items.title: CSF: Contextual Safety Filtering for Motion Generators
items.summary: Text-conditioned motion generators produce trackable whole-body motion, but they have no notion of scene-dependent safety: the same action may target an object or a person. Existing safeguards either inspect the prompt, require labeled motion data, or enforce geometric constraints; therefore, they do not directly account for how scene context changes a motion's meaning. items.title: On the estimation and validity of AI time horizons---a statistical look at the METR plot
items.summary: METR's 50\% time horizon measures the human completion time of software tasks that an AI solves with 50\% probability, allowing AI capabilities to be expressed in interpretable units. On 228 tasks and 26 AIs, we recompute the time horizons using splines and item-response theory to relax the assumption that the AI difficulty of a task depends linearly on the log of human time. items.summary: General-purpose robots must perform a wide range of tasks from agile locomotion to dexterous manipulation. While sim-to-real reinforcement learning (RL) has proven to be a useful tool for this goal, current RL pipelines depend on engineering-heavy, per-task structural priors such as shaped rewards and demonstrations. items.title: BrickBench: Evaluating Agentic Brick Design
items.summary: We propose BrickBench, a benchmark for agentic text-conditioned LEGO-set design. Given a prompt, an agent is tasked with producing an assembly that not only satisfies semantic and design criteria, but that can also be physically built. To do so, it must select parts from a discrete library and reason jointly about local and global constraints. We score validity, alignment, and design across three…

items.title: One Block, Multiple Depths: Recurrent Vision Transformers with Depth-Programmed Experts
items.summary: In this work, we show that a single Transformer block, applied recurrently, can match the accuracy of a full-depth vision encoder at comparable inference FLOPs without intermediate feature distillation. reViT restores depth-specific transformations by representing the FFN at each recurrent depth as a convex combination of a small shared expert bank. items.title: Bi-FORK: Generative Modeling of High-Dimensional Bifurcating Systems
items.summary: Bifurcations are ubiquitous in physical systems, from structural buckling to fluid and climate dynamics, yet they remain largely unexplored in deep learning. At a symmetry-breaking bifurcation, a single input admits multiple equally valid solutions, violating the one-to-one assumption underlying most learned physical surrogates. items.title: Caught in the Act: Probes Effectively Detect Sabotage and Catch Unverbalized Deception
items.summary: Recent incidents have highlighted the challenge of monitoring LLM agents and the danger of models deceiving people. We show that white-box deception detection via probes can be scaled up to frontier monitoring settings by collecting the largest deception dataset to date for training probes and introducing a novel probe architecture which can aggregate information across many layers and tokens…

items.title: Rounding in Preconditioner Space: Redesigning 4-bit AdamW Optimizer-State Quantization
items.summary: Quantizing AdamW's optimizer states reduces persistent storage, but quantization errors propagate through the moment recurrences and perturb subsequent adaptive updates. We redesign 4-bit optimizer-state quantization for AdamW from the perspective of \emph{rounding space}: the coordinate in which a quantizer chooses between adjacent reconstruction levels. items.title: Density Ratio Estimation with Stein Displacement Fields
items.summary: Density ratios quantify distribution shift from a probability-mass point of view, whereas displacement fields describe, from a dynamical point of view, how one distribution is transported onto another. items.title: Ecology of AI Agents: Collaboration Creates a Population Threshold for Takeoff
items.summary: AI agents can now conduct real-world cyberattacks, scale up capabilities with the number of agents, and collectively pursue misaligned goals to obtain rewards. items.title: VioLA: Learning Generalist Humanoid Control Policies from Human Data
items.summary: Teaching a humanoid to follow instructions with its whole body runs into two obstacles. Its action space is large and tightly coupled: legs, arms, and fingers must move together while the robot keeps its balance, which makes joint-level actions hard to learn. items.title: FAITH: Feasibility-Aware Safety-Filtered RL for High-Dimensional Systems
items.summary: Safe reinforcement learning commonly places safety and task performance in the same policy objective, where they can introduce competing updates. items.title: Toward Joint Optimization of Circuit Depth and Training Data Size in Adaptively Grown Quantum Classifiers
items.summary: Building a quantum model involves a tradeoff: how complex the circuit should be, and how much training data it needs. Caro et al. show that models with fewer trainable gates need less training data to generalize well. Q-FLAIR shows that a quantum feature-map circuit can be grown gate-by-gate, stopping once further growth stops improving the training loss. We ask whether these two results combine…

items.title: FastBench: Can Streaming VLMs Perceive High-Dynamic Real-World Streams?
items.summary: Streaming Video Large Language Models (VLMs) enable continuous video understanding, yet existing benchmarks focus on low-dynamic scenarios. Under bounded context budgets, models must balance temporal history, spatial resolution, and temporal granularity; sparse sampling at 1--2 FPS misses fast events. items.summary: A generalist robot should not only perform diverse tasks but also improve through experience, turning what it learns during execution into capabilities that later tasks can reuse. items.summary: Dense correspondence matching has historically been bounded by simplifying spatio-temporal priors, such as smooth motion and rigid geometry. While effective for classical tasks, these assumptions break down in image editing and reference-guided generation (IEG), where transformations can preserve visual identity while breaking physical continuity. items.title: A Unified Bellman Operator for Safety-Critical Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Reinforcement learning in safety-critical domains requires maximizing task performance while strictly adhering to safety constraints. items.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) struggle with spatial, embodied, physical, and temporal reasoning. items.summary: Generating realistic human-object interactions (HOI) in complex 3D scenes requires two complementary capabilities: reasoning about interaction feasibility in the environment and synthesizing realistic human-object motion.
